The petitioner filed this petition U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1988 for claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/-.
2.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioner is that, on 13-09-2024 at about 12.20 p.m. she was riding her Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-05/ER-6813 on the extreme left side of Kanakapura Main Road, J.P. Nagar 1st Phase, Bangalore and she reached near Banashankari Metro Station, wherein all of a sudden a Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-05/AC-7627 driven by its driver, in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger the human life, came at high speed and dashed against the petitioner's Scooter from behind, caused the accident, due to forced impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries her right hand, chest and ankle.
3. Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was taken to Sevakshethra hospital for first aid,
then she was shifted to KIMS Hospital, Bangalore, wherein she was treated as an inpatient.
It is further stated that, the petitioner is still bed ridden and under treatment, so far has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical and other expenses.
She has to undertake further treatment and has to incur future medical expenses also, she has suffered permanent disability, she is unable to lead a normal life as earlier.

4. It is further stated that prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy and aged about 34 years, she was working as a Ladies Tailor and running a provision store and earning Rs.45,000/-
p.m.
Due to the injuries, she was not doing as earlier and she is facing great financial difficulties.

5. It is stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence act of the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-05/AC-7627, against whom the Jayanagar Traffic Police have registered the case in Cr.No.121/2024.
Hence, respondent No.1 being the Insurer and respondent No.2 being the Owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

Hence,
prayed to allow the petition.

6. In pursuance to the notice, respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before the Court, but,
respondent 2 has not filed objections to the main petition.
7. Respondent No.1/Insurance Company has filed its objection to the main petition and contended that, the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
It is further contended that, it has admitted the issuance of insurance policy and it was in force as on the date of accident.

It is further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle did not have effective and valid DL to drive the Ayisha vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138717793/
2 same and as such respondent No.1 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.

sentences.text: It is further contended that, there was no negligence on the part of the alleged driver of the alleged insured vehicle in issue as he was proceeding with due care and cautious by following traffic rules and regulations.
On the contrary, it is specifically submitted that the alleged accident occurred due to the sole negligence of the petitioner herself.

Further, Respondent No.2 has denied the accident, age,
income and also the amount spent towards medical expenses by the petitioner.
It has further contended that the compensation and interest claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.

8. On basis of the pleadings and materials, this Tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1) Whether petitioner proves that on 13-09- 2024 at about 12.20 PM, she was riding a Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA- 05/ER-6813 on Kanakapura Main Road, J.P. Nagar 1st Phase, Bangalore and reached near Banashankari Metro Station, at that time, the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-05/AC-7627 drove the same, in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger the human life, came at high speed, dashed against the petitioner's Scooter from behind and caused the accident, due to forced impact the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
if so, what is the quantum and from whom?
3 . What order or award?

9. In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 17 documents as per Ex.P.1 to 17 and got examined the Doctor as PW.2 and got marked 02 documents as per Ex.P.18 and P.19.
The petitioner got examined the Medical Record Officer as PW.3 and got marked 04 documents as per Ex.P.20 to P.23.
On the other hand, the respondents have not examined any oral evidence and not marked any documents on their sides.
10. Heard the arguments of both sides and perused the materials available on hand.

The Ld. Counsel for the petitioner has relied upon a judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2011 ACJ 1699,
between Rudra Vs. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Co. Ltd., & Another.

sentences.text: 3 REASONS 12. ISSUE No.1:

The petitioner filed this petition against the respondents for claiming compensation due to injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident, that occurred on 13-09-2024.
13.
The petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and reiterated the entire contention of petition and got marked 17 documents as Ex.P.1 to 17.
Ex.P.1 is the copy of F.I.R. Ex.P.2 is the copy of Complaint,

Ex.P.3 is the copy of Sketch, Ex.P.4 is the copy of Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.5 is the copy of IMV Report,
Ex.P.6 is the copy of Wound Certificate, Ex.P.7 is the copy of Notice U/Sec.133 of MV Act, Ex.P.8 is the Reply to the Notice, Ex.P.9 is the copy of Charge Sheet, Ex.P.10 is the Discharge Summary,
Ex.P.11 is the OPD Cards, Ex.P.12 is the copy of Aadhar Card of the petitioner, Ex.P.13 is the Advance cum Final Settlement Receipts, Ex.P.14 is the Medical Bills, Ex.P.15 is the Prescriptions,
Ex.P.16 is the Colour Photos with CD and Ex.P.17 is the X-ray Films.
In the cross-examination she has stated that, the accident was caused by the Lorry, presently she is not doing any work.
Further denied that, the accident took place due to her negligence.
14. The petitioner got examined Dr. S.A. Somashekara, who is an Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bangalore is examined as PW.2 and got marked 02 documents as Ex.P.18 and 19.
Ex.P.18 is the OPD Book and Ex.P.19 is the X-ray.
15. The petitioner got examined the Medical Record Technician of KIMS Hospital, Bangalore as PW.3 and got marked 04 documents as Ex.P.20 to 23.
Ex.P.20 is the Authorization Letter, Ex.P.21 is the copy of MLC, Ex.P.22 is the Inpatient Records and Ex.P.23 is the X-ray.
16. Per contra, the respondents have not adduced any evidence and got marked no documents on their side.

17. On perusal of Ex.P.1 the FIR, Ex.P.2 the Complaint, Ex.P.3-the Spot Sketch, Ex.P.4 the Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.5 the IMV Report, Ex.P.7 the Notice U/Sec.133 of MV Act, Ex.P.8 the Reply to the Notice and Ex.P.9 Charge Sheet, it appears that, the offending Lorry has hit the petitioner from back side while petitioner was moving on the left of the road and offending Lorry came towards left side from the right side of the road and dashed to the petitioner's motorcycle.

Hence, it appears that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-05/AC-7627, so it clearly indicates that the offending vehicle involved in the accident.

Further on perusal of charge sheet it discloses that, the Jayanagar Traffic Police have filed the case against the rider of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-05/AC-762 for the offence punishable U/Sec.281 and 125(B) of BNS r/w Sec.187 and 134(A & B) of MV Act.
18.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others held that, in the petition for compensation U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act.1988 the petitioner has to prove the incident only on the preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt is not required.

sentences.text: After careful scrutiny of Ex.P.1 the copy of FIR, Ex.P.2 the copy of Complaint, Ex.P.3-Copy of spot Sketch, Ex.P.4 the copy of Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.5-the copy of IMV Report, Ex.P.6 the copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.7 the copy of Notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act, Ex.P.8 the copy of reply to the notice and Ex.P.9 the copy of charge sheet, it appears that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-05/ AC-762.
Hence, this Tribunal answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
20. ISSUE No.2:-
The petitioner claiming the compensation amount of Rs.15,00,000/- with respect to injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.
The petitioner produced wound certificate at Ex.P.6 and Ex.P.10 discharge summary issued by KIMS Hospital, Bangalore and prayed to award compensation amount.
The respondents not disputed the said documents.
On perusal of the Wound Certificate at Ex.P.6, it is discloses that the petitioner has sustained (1) Tenderness and Swelling present over right forearm region, multiple abrasions present.
(2) Abrasion present over right lateral malleoli region.
X-ray dtd:13-09-2024 of right forearm shows fracture of mid shaft of radius with displacement of distal fracture fragment medially.
On perusal of the said injuries, the Doctor has opinion that the injury No.1 is grievous in nature and injury No.2 is simple in nature.

Further, on perusal of Ex.P.10 discharge summary, wherein the diagnosis that, post traumatic fracture of middle 1/3rd shaft of right radius procedure and ORIF with plate and screws (LC DCP) to right radius on 14-09- 2024 and admitted on 13-09-2024 and discharged on 17- 09-2024.

Therefore, taking all these facts and nature of injuries, as petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and admitted in the hospital, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of Rs.50,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of pain and suffering.
21. The petitioner produced medical bills, which is marked as Ex.P.14.
As per the said bills, the petitioner has spent Rs.48,392/- towards medical expenses.
The respondents have not made out any grounds to disbelieve the medical bills.

On perusal of the said medical bills and also considering the bills and also treatment taken by the petitioner in the hospital, the petitioner is entitled to claim the medical bills amount of Rs.48,392/- under the head of medical expenditure.
22. As per Ex.P.10 discharge summary the petitioner took treatment at KIMS Hospital, Bangalore from 13-09-2024 to 17-09-2024 i.e., for 05 days.

Therefore, by considering the period of treatment taken as inpatient this tribunal awarded reasonable compensation of Rs.5,000/- under the head Transportation, food, Nourishment and conveyance charges.
23. The petitioner contended that, due to injuries she was suffering from pain and mental agony and she is unable to carry on his day to day activities which she used to do prior to the accident.
To prove the assessment of disability, the petitioner got examined one Dr. S.A. Somashekara as PW-2.

In the chief examination affidavit PW.2 deposed that, the petitioner came to him for assessment of disability purpose and on examination he found that, she has suffered (a) Post traumatic displaced fracture of middle third of shaft of right radius and (b) Right rib fractures and she underwent surgery of ORIF with plate and screws to right radius under GA on 14-09- 2024.
Now she complaints of pain and difficulty in using right upper limb for activities of daily living and she gives history of inability to lift weight.
On examination that, wasting of right arm and diffuse swelling of right forearm is seen and surgical scar and keloids are seen over volar aspect of right forearm.

He Ayisha vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138717793/
5 examined the petitioner clinically and radiologically and assessed the total disability of the right upper limb at 30.5% and the whole body disability of the petitioner at 15.25%.

entities.text: He Ayisha vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the cross- examination admitted that, he is not the treated doctor, he examined the petitioner first time on 24-07-2025 only to assess the disability and he has seen the copy of wound certificate and discharge summary.
The fractures are united.
Only implants have to be removed.
However, by considering the nature of the wounds, condition of the petitioner and evidence of the doctor this Tribunal has considered the disability of the Petitioner at 11% to the whole body.

24. The petitioner stated that, at the time of accident she was aged about 34 years and she was working as Tailoring and also running a provision store and she used to earn a sum of Rs.45,000/-p.m. and due to injuries sustained in the accident, she cannot do any work as earlier.
The petitioner has not produced any documents to prove her income and avocation.
Therefore, in present days the coolie worker get Rs.500/- to Rs.600/- per day.
This accident is of the year 2024.

However, by considering the age and occupation of petitioner this Tribunal taken the monthly income of the petitioner at Rs.16,500/-.
25.
As per Ex.P.12 Notarized Copy of Adhar Card, the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 27-06-1990.
Therefore, age of the Petitioner is taken as 34 years at the time of accident.

Then the proper multiplier applicable is 16 which comes as follows:
Rs.16,500 x 12 x 16 x 11% = Rs.3,48,480/-
Hence, this Tribunal award Rs.3,48,480/- under the head loss of future earning capacity on account of disability.
26. The petitioner also sought for expenses towards future medicine for further treatment.
In the chief- examination affidavit the petitioner deposed that, she is forced to spent huge amount for future medication for Rs.60,000/-.
PW.2 doctor deposed in the chief affidavit that, the petitioner needs another surgery for the removal of implant and the estimate of said surgery is around Rs.40,000/-.
In the cross-examination the PW.2 admitted that he had not treated the petitioner and fractures are united.

However, by considering the age and nature of injuries and evidence of the doctor, this Tribunal has award reasonable compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head future medical expenses (Which does not carry any interest).

27. The petitioner stated that, prior to the accident she was working as Tailor and also running a provision store and she used to earn a sum of Rs.45,000/-p.m. and due to injuries sustained in the accident, she is unable to attend the work and facing financial difficulties.
The petitioner had not produced any documents to prove her income and avocation.
This accident occurred in the year 2024.

However, by considering the age and nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, this Tribunal awarded reasonable compensation amount of Rs.30,000/- under the head loss of income during laid up period.

sentences.text: The petitioner sustained grievous injury as shown in the wound certificate.
The petitioner was doing Tailoring and also running a provision store and due to accidental injuries her routine work was hampered for some days.

Therefore, by considering this aspect and the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, this tribunal awarded the amount of Rs.30,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of loss of amenities.

29. Considering oral evidence coupled with documentary evidence, it is just and proper to grant compensation as follows:

 period.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,51,872/-.
30. Interest:

In so far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, in MFA.No.103557/2016 (between Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20- 03-2018) the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru has held that as per Sec.34 of CPC the rate of interest that can be awarded on Judgments cannot be more than 6% p.a. and that since Sec.149 of M.V. Act provides for the interest on Judgments, the interest to be awarded in claim petitions has to be 6% p.a.
and not more than that.

entities.text: Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20- 03-2018
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, this Tribunal has hold that the petitioner is entitled for interest @6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of payment.

sentences.text: Respondent No.1 is the Insurer and respondent No.2 is the RC Owner of the offending Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-05/AC-7627.

As discussed in the Issue No.1 it is proved that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle, hence Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Further, the Respondent No.1 being Insurer of the offending vehicle is primarily held liable to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioner.
Accordingly, this Tribunal answered Issue No.2 in the Partly Affirmative.
32. ISSUE No.3:

For the foregoing reasons, this Tribunal proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost as hereunder.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.5,51,872/- with interest @ 6% p.a.,(excluding future medical expenses) from the date of petition till its realization.
Respondent No.1 & 2 jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Further, Respondent No.1 being Insurer of the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6% interest within 60 days, from the date of this order.
After deposit, entire compensation amount shall be released in favour of the petitioner with proper identification.
(As petitioner has to incur some more amount for her future treatment) Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.

Further on perusal of charge sheet it discloses that, the Jayanagar Traffic Police have filed the case against the rider of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-05/AC-762 for the offence punishable U/Sec.281 and 125(B) of BNS r/w Sec.187 and 134(A & B) of MV Act.
18.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others held that, in the petition for compensation U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act.1988 the petitioner has to prove the incident only on the preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt is not required.
Ayisha vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138717793/
4 19.
Therefore, taking all these facts and nature of injuries, as petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and admitted in the hospital, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of Rs.50,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of pain and suffering.
In the cross- examination admitted that, he is not the treated doctor, he examined the petitioner first time on 24-07-2025 only to assess the disability and he has seen the copy of wound certificate and discharge summary.
However, by considering the age and nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, this Tribunal awarded reasonable compensation amount of Rs.30,000/- under the head loss of income during laid up period.
Ayisha vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138717793/
6 28.
In so far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, in MFA.No.103557/2016 (between Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20- 03-2018) the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru has held that as per Sec.34 of CPC the rate of interest that can be awarded on Judgments cannot be more than 6% p.a. and that since Sec.149 of M.V. Act provides for the interest on Judgments, the interest to be awarded in claim petitions has to be 6% p.a.
and not more than that.
Hence, this Tribunal has hold that the petitioner is entitled for interest @6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of payment.
31. Liability:-
Ayisha vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138717793/
7
Respondent No.1 is the Insurer and respondent No.2 is the RC Owner of the offending Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-05/AC-7627.
As discussed in the Issue No.1 it is proved that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle, hence Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
